title: Harden product image pipeline and replace forged/invalid inventory images
description:
Replace bad product main images through three fast, non-blocking pipelines.

## Pipeline 1 - Detect
Open a target localhost URL and use an AI agent to identify products with bad main images. Output a focused list of products needing replacement.

## Pipeline 2 - Source
For each product in the list, find a replacement main image on the internet.

## Pipeline 3 - Replace
Process each sourced image through background removal and size management, then patch the bad main image in Sanity with the clean, properly-sized replacement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Detection pipeline outputs a list of products with bad main images.
- [ ] Sourcing pipeline finds a replacement image for each listed product.
- [ ] Replacement pipeline produces clean, properly-sized images and patches Sanity.
- [ ] Re-run of detection pipeline shows zero products with bad main images.

title: Regression: Hero image hotspot/objectPosition broken after RSC loader fix
notes:
## Frame — 2026-06-13

### Root Cause (Critical Intelligence)


ext.config.ts sets images.loader: 'custom' + loaderFile: './lib/utils/sanityImageLoader.ts' — this makes sanityImageLoader the **global default loader** for every <Image> in the project.

- The explicit loader={sanityImageLoader} props on all Server Components were **redundant** — not needed
- They also caused the React 19 RSC violation (functions can't cross Server→Client boundary)
- Today's fix added a SanityImage use client wrapper that re-applies the explicit loader prop
- This wrapper approach conflicts with the global loaderFile config, breaking the hero's objectPosition/hotspot CSS

**Correct fix**: simply REMOVE the explicit loader prop from all Server Components. The global loaderFile config already applies sanityImageLoader to every <Image>. Zero wrapper needed. Zero RSC violation. Zero regression.

### Objective
Restore hero hotspot/objectPosition to its pre-regression state by reverting the SanityImage wrapper approach and instead removing the now-unnecessary explicit loader props from all 18 Server Components.

### Happy Path (implement THIS first)

#### Tasks
1. pp/components/ui/sanity-image/SanityImage.tsx — Simplify wrapper: remove explicit loader={sanityImageLoader} prop (global config handles it), OR delete entirely if no remaining callers
2. pp/components/features/homepage/hero/Hero.tsx — Revert: replace <SanityImage> with <Image> from next/image (no loader prop needed), restore SanityImage as SanityImageData type alias back to SanityImage
3. All 17 remaining Server Components that were changed today — Revert: replace <SanityImage> with <Image> from next/image (no loader prop). Keep existing className/fill/style/sizes/quality props exactly as-is
4. Client Components (ImageGallery, BasketItem, ProductImage, RelatedProducts, CarouselMediaBox) — Leave untouched. Their explicit loader prop is redundant but harmless in client context

#### Acceptance
- [ ] Live check: hero section on localhost shows full headphones with correct hotspot crop matching production (sanglogium.com) — earpad detail visible, not just the headband arc
- [ ] grep -r 'loader={sanityImageLoader}' app/ — zero matches in Server Components (files without 'use client')
- [ ] 
pm run dev — zero RSC 'Functions cannot be passed' errors in console
- [ ] SanityImage.tsx wrapper either deleted or simplified to NOT pass explicit loader (since global loaderFile already does it)

### Edge Cases Path — LOCKED until happy path passes

#### Known concerns
- SegmentTitle.tsx uses /logo-orbit.svg (local static path) — sanityImageLoader passes through '/' paths, no change needed
- Searchbar.tsx uses static SVG import — same passthrough behavior, no issue
- Client Components currently passing explicit loader — redundant but safe, no change needed unless consistency is desired

description:
PM Evaluation Questions — Search Happy Path (Autocomplete + Search Page)
9 questions. Any NO = not professional.

Prerequisite
1. Is the search input visible and accessible from every page of the store (persistent header nav)?

Autocomplete
2. Does the autocomplete overlay appear after the user types ≥2 characters?

3. Do the suggestions always reflect what the user currently has typed — not a stale result from a previous (shorter) query?

4. Does each autocomplete suggestion show at minimum: product name + price?

5. Does selecting a suggestion — by click or by keyboard (↑/↓ to highlight, Enter to confirm) — navigate to the correct product page?

6. Does the "View all results for X" option at the bottom of the overlay navigate to the search results page for that exact query?

Search Results Page
7. Does the search results page display products that are relevant to the submitted query?

8. Does each result card show at minimum: product image, product name, and price?

9. Does the page heading reflect the query that was searched, and is the total result count visible?

Mobile
11. on mobile, does clicking any result from autocomplete lead to respective product page? 
12. on mobile, does clicking results page, navigate to seearch results page with adequate content based on query?
notes:
PM EVALUATION 2026-06-10:

Desktop Autocomplete (Q2-Q6): 6x PASS
- Overlay appears on >=2 chars: YES
- No stale suggestions: YES
- Name + price visible: YES
- Click/keyboard selection navigates: YES
- View all results link works: YES

Search Results Page (Q7-Q9): 3x PASS
- Relevant products: YES
- Image + name + price: YES
- Heading reflects query + count visible: YES

Mobile (Q10-Q12): 1x PASS, 2x FAIL
- Q10: Autocomplete overlay appears: YES
- Q11: Clicking autocomplete result navigates: NO (nothing happens, black screen)
- Q12: Search results page from View all results: NO (nothing happens, black screen)

BLOCKER: Mobile search is non-functional. Scope 1 NOT complete.

## Frame Ôö£├ÂÔö£├ºÔö£├é 2026-06-10

### Objective
Mobile search clicks (autocomplete items + View all results) must navigate to the correct page and dismiss the mobile overlay. Desktop behavior already works.

### Root Cause
1. **containerRef leak in handleClickOutside** (SearchField.tsx:109-117): containerRef is attached only to the desktop div (hidden sm:block). On mobile, containerRef.current still references the hidden desktop div. Every click inside the mobile overlay is outside this hidden div, so closeOverlay() fires on mousedown Ôö£├ÂÔö£├ºÔö£├é closing the autocomplete list but NOT the mobile overlay.
2. **Product Link missing explicit onClick** (AutocompleteItem.tsx:26): The product Link has NO onClick prop. Overlay cleanup (setMobileExpanded(false)) relies entirely on event bubbling to the ul's onClick={onItemClick}. If Next.js Link calls e.stopPropagation() or the event chain breaks, cleanup never runs.
3. **Mobile overlay persistence risk**: SearchField lives in Header (layout component), which persists across Next.js App Router navigation. If mobileExpanded is not explicitly set to  alse, the  ixed inset-0 z-[60] bg-brand-900 overlay stays mounted, covering the entire viewport Ôö£├ÂÔö£├ºÔö£├é producing the reported 'black screen'.

### Happy Path ├ö├ç├Â IMPLEMENTED 2026-06-10

#### Tasks
1. [x] SearchField.tsx ├ö├ç├Â handleClickOutside now skips when mobileExpanded is true
2. [x] AutocompleteItem.tsx ├ö├ç├Â Added onClick?: () => void prop, passed to Link`n3. [x] AutocompleteOverlay.tsx ├ö├ç├Â Passes onItemClick to each AutocompleteItem as onClick, removed redundant ul onClick

2. **pp/components/features/search/AutocompleteItem.tsx** Ôö£├ÂÔö£├ºÔö£├é Add onClick?: () => void prop. Pass it to the Link component as onClick={onClick}. This makes cleanup explicit on the product Link itself, removing reliance on event bubbling.

title: IEMs gallery `IemsGallery` + `IemCard` layout is broken below `xs` (475 px)
description:
## Problem

At 320–474 px the IEMs gallery renders as a 2-column grid, the brand text is 10 px, and the in-basket stepper is forced to 32×32 px / 28 px, all below the readable/usable thresholds for small phones:

- `IemsGallery.tsx:27` uses `grid-cols-2` as the unprefixed, mobile-first default, so the grid is 2 columns below `xs`.
- `IemCard.tsx:43` sets the brand `span` to `text-tiny ... xs:text-small`; the mobile-first default is `text-tiny` (10 px), so below `xs` the brand text is 10 px.
- `IemCard.tsx:64-66` passes `w-8 h-8` and `w-7` className overrides to `BasketControls`, overriding the component's default `h-11 w-11 min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]` size classes (`BasketControls.tsx:98, 102, 108`) and shrinking the increment/decrement buttons to 32×32 px and the quantity display to 28 px wide.

## Value

Small-phone users (320–474 px) are a material mobile segment; the 2-column grid, 10 px brand text, and sub-44×44 px basket stepper touch targets directly hurt mobile checkout conversion and WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size accessibility.

## Scope

- `IemsGallery.tsx:27` — change the grid class from `grid grid-cols-2 gap-x-4 gap-y-8 md:grid-cols-4 md:gap-x-8 md:gap-y-12` to `grid grid-cols-1 gap-x-4 gap-y-8 xs:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 md:gap-x-8 md:gap-y-12`. Tailwind is mobile-first: the unprefixed `grid-cols-1` targets <475 px; `xs:grid-cols-2` targets ≥475 px (`tailwind.config.ts:494` sets `xs: "475px"`).
- `IemCard.tsx:43` — change the brand `span` class from `text-tiny ... xs:text-small` to `text-small`. The existing `xs:text-small` token is redundant once the default is `text-small`; remove it. Unprefixed `text-small` (12 px) now applies below `xs`.
- `IemCard.tsx:64` — change `decrementClassName` to `btn-secondary h-11 w-11 min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] flex items-center justify-center`.
- `IemCard.tsx:65` — change `incrementClassName` to `btn-secondary h-11 w-11 min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] flex items-center justify-center disabled:opacity-50`.
- `IemCard.tsx:66` — change `quantityClassName` to `h-11 w-11 min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] flex items-center justify-center text-center type-body text-primary tabular-nums`. The quantity `span` needs `flex items-center justify-center` so the number stays vertically centered inside the 44×44 box.

## Out of scope

- 475 px and above (handled by `sang-logium-fz2` and later beads).
- Product images, hover states, or Playwright tests.
- The initial-state "Add to Cart" button (`addClassName` prop), the bottom "View All In-Ear Monitors" link in `IemsGallery.tsx:39-44`, and the section header (`IemsGalleryHeader.tsx` / `SectionHeader.tsx`); the gallery header and bottom link already use `whitespace-nowrap`, and there is no concrete evidence of overflow at these viewports.
- Sibling card components (`AccessoryCard.tsx`, `DacCard.tsx`, `ProductCard.tsx`, `Featured.tsx`, `ProductInfo.tsx`) that share the same small stepper pattern.
- Changes to `BasketControls.tsx` itself; the defaults already provide 44×44 px, so the fix is only in the `IemCard` className props.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `IemsGallery.tsx:27` contains `grid-cols-1 xs:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4`.
- [ ] `IemCard.tsx:43` brand `span` has `text-small` and does not contain `text-tiny` or `xs:text-small`.
- [ ] `IemCard.tsx:64` `decrementClassName` includes `h-11 w-11 min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]` and no `w-8 h-8`.
- [ ] `IemCard.tsx:65` `incrementClassName` includes `h-11 w-11 min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]` and no `w-8 h-8`.
- [ ] `IemCard.tsx:66` `quantityClassName` includes `h-11 w-11 min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]` and no `w-7`.
- [ ] Manual check at 320 px, 360 px, and 414 px shows the gallery in a single column, brand text at 12 px, and all basket stepper elements (decrement, quantity, increment) at 44×44 px or larger.
- [ ] The `+`, `−`, and quantity number remain horizontally and vertically centered.
- [ ] Product name and price row do not overflow horizontally at 320 px, 360 px, or 414 px.
- [ ] No horizontal overflow or layout shift at 1280 px.

## Verification

Manual responsive check in the browser at 320 px, 360 px, 414 px, and 1280 px.

## Related files

- `app/components/features/homepage/iems-gallery/IemsGallery.tsx`
- `app/components/features/homepage/iems-gallery/IemCard.tsx`
- `app/components/features/basket/BasketControls.tsx`
- `tailwind.config.ts`

## Dependencies

None.

## Prerequisites

- Dev server running on the project port (e.g., `localhost:3000`) with the homepage IEMs gallery populated.
- Browser dev tools with viewport/device emulation at the listed widths.
- At least one IEM product in the basket (or the ability to add one via the UI) so the increment/decrement/quantity stepper is visible; the initial "Add to Cart" state is out of scope for this bead.

title: IemsGallery.tsx:27 `xs:grid-cols-2` makes IEMs cards cramped at 475–767 px
description:
## Problem

`IemsGallery.tsx:27` uses the class string `grid grid-cols-1 gap-x-4 gap-y-8 xs:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 md:gap-x-8 md:gap-y-12`. Because Tailwind is mobile-first and `xs` is set to `475px` in `tailwind.config.ts:494`, this renders the IEMs gallery in 2 columns from 475 px up to the default `md` breakpoint (768 px). At the lower end of that range the cards are too narrow for the product name, the price row, and the 44×44 px basket controls; the price/basket row can collide.

## Value

Portrait mobile and small-tablet users (475–767 px) are a meaningful traffic segment; cramped cards reduce scanability and basket-control tap reliability, directly lowering mobile conversion.

## Scope

- `IemsGallery.tsx:27` — change the grid class from `grid grid-cols-1 gap-x-4 gap-y-8 xs:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-4 md:gap-x-8 md:gap-y-12` to `grid grid-cols-1 gap-x-4 gap-y-8 md:grid-cols-4 md:gap-x-8 md:gap-y-12`.
  - Tailwind is mobile-first; the unprefixed `grid-cols-1` now applies below `md` (768 px).
  - `xs: \"475px\"` in `tailwind.config.ts:494`; removing `xs:grid-cols-2` eliminates 2-column cards in the 475–767 px range.

## Out of scope

- Below 475 px (already 1 column) and 768 px+ (already 4 columns via `md:grid-cols-4`).
- `IemCard.tsx`, `IemsGalleryHeader.tsx`, or shared `SectionHeader.tsx`.
- Product images, hover states, or Playwright tests.
- Sibling card components.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `IemsGallery.tsx:27` does not contain `xs:grid-cols-2`.
- [ ] `IemsGallery.tsx:27` still contains `grid-cols-1` and `md:grid-cols-4`.
- [ ] Manual check at 475 px, 640 px, and 767 px shows the gallery as a single column.
- [ ] Product name and price/basket row do not overflow horizontally at 475 px, 640 px, or 767 px.

title: IEMs gallery vertical rhythm is compressed on 1024+ short viewports
description:
## Problem

On `lg-touch` (≥1024 px width, ≤850 px height) the section padding and card gaps compress the vertical rhythm, making the section feel crowded.

## Value

Short-height desktop/laptop users see a cramped section; fixing it improves perceived quality and scrollability.

## Scope

- `IemsGallery.tsx`: tune `lg-touch:` padding and gaps.
- `IemCard.tsx`: verify cards are not vertically compressed; tweak only if needed.

## Out of scope

- Below 1024 px.
- Changing column count.
- Product images.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All `## Acceptance` criteria are checked off.
- [ ] Manual verification at 1024×600, 1280×700, and 1366×768 shows comfortable vertical rhythm.
- [ ] No regression at 1280×900 or 375 px.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Vertical rhythm at `lg-touch` is comfortable; no excessive whitespace or crowding.
- [ ] Cards remain aligned and images visible.
- [ ] No horizontal overflow.
- [ ] Section header and “View All” are not pushed or overlapping.

## Verification

Manual responsive check at 1024×600, 1280×700, and 1366×768.
